entities.name: Thutmose IV
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Thutmose IV was the 8th Pharaoh of the 18th Dynasty of Egypt, who ruled from circa 1400 to 1389 BCE, leaving a significant mark on the political and cultural landscape of the ancient Near East.

Born to Amenhotep II and Tiaa, Thutmose IV ascended to the throne at a young age and went on to establish a period of relative peace and prosperity, marked by significant military campaigns and the establishment of trade networks across Africa and the Eastern Mediterranean.

One of his most notable achievements was the construction of the magnificent temple complex at Karnak, one of the largest and most impressive in Egypt, which served as a testament to his wealth and power.

Thutmose IV's legacy extends beyond his own reign, as his successor, Akhenaten, would go on to introduce radical reforms and the worship of a single, monotheistic deity, Aten.

Thutmose IV's prenomen, Menkheperure, means 'Established in forms is Re,' a reflection of his devotion to the Egyptian sun god, Ra.
